name: Wonderchat
tagline: A tiny, bootstrapped Singapore team's no-code AI chatbot builder — thin on independent reviews, but priced with a real resolution-based free tier.
tldr: Wonderchat is a no-code AI chatbot builder that trains a support agent on your website, documents, and uploaded files, with a resolution-based (not just message-based) usage model.

Pricing runs Free (10 resolutions/mo, 1 agent) through Basic ($124/mo, 1,000 resolutions), Turbo ($417/mo, 5,000 resolutions, voice agent, helpdesk integrations), and Enterprise (from $1,499/mo, SOC 2 & HIPAA, SSO, SMS/phone agents).
Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Singapore, led by CEO Vera Sun; the company is bootstrapped with no outside funding and reportedly runs with an extremely small team (around 2 people).

Independent review presence is thin — G2 shows only a handful of reviews (around 5.0/5 from roughly 3 reviews) and Capterra currently shows no reviews at all, which is itself worth flagging to any buyer expecting the review depth of a Chatbase or Tidio.
The Turbo tier's inclusion of a voice agent and helpdesk integrations is notable at a comparatively low $417/mo relative to competitors gating similar features behind enterprise-only custom pricing.
keyFeatures: Resolution-based usage metering (distinct from raw message counts) across all paid tiers, plus a separate monthly credit pool
Self-improving AI agents on the Basic tier and above, refining answers based on real conversation history
Voice agent capability included at the Turbo tier ($417/mo), notably lower-priced than many competitors' voice add-ons
Helpdesk integrations and advanced analytics from Turbo tier upward
Human handover built into every tier, including Free, for escalating conversations the AI can't resolve
Multiple AI Agents per workspace (2 on Basic, 4 on Turbo) for running separate bots per use case or brand
SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance, SSO, and SMS/phone agents reserved for the Enterprise tier
Chat workflows for structuring multi-step conversation logic beyond simple Q&A retrieval

faq.question: How is Wonderchat priced?
faq.answer: By monthly resolutions (successfully handled conversations) plus a credit pool: Free (10 resolutions), Basic $124/mo (1,000 resolutions, 2 AI Agents), Turbo $417/mo (5,000 resolutions, voice agent, helpdesk integrations), and Enterprise from $1,499/mo (custom capacity, SOC 2/HIPAA, SSO).

faq.question: Does Wonderchat support voice, not just text chat?
faq.answer: Yes — a voice agent is included starting at the Turbo tier ($417/mo), and SMS/phone agents are available at the Enterprise tier, which is broader channel coverage than several similarly-priced AI chatbot competitors.

faq.question: How established is Wonderchat as a company?
faq.answer: It's a small, bootstrapped team (reportedly around 2 people) founded in 2023 in Singapore with no outside funding — buyers should weigh that against the vendor stability of larger, better-funded competitors.

faq.question: How many independent reviews does Wonderchat have?
faq.answer: Very few as of this writing — G2 shows only a handful of reviews and does not have enough volume to generate its standard buying-insight summary, and Capterra currently lists no reviews at all. Treat any rating derived from this small a sample with appropriate caution.

faq.question: What's the free plan good for?
faq.answer: The Free tier includes 10 resolutions/month, 1 AI Agent, human handover, and an embeddable widget — enough to trial the product on a low-traffic site, but not a viable long-term free option for an active support inbox.

scorecard.note: Reviewers describe training and deploying an assistant from business documents as quick and technically uncomplicated.
Self-improving agents and resolution-based metering suggest a thoughtful design, but the very small independent review base makes real-world AI quality hard to verify confidently.
Voice agent at a comparatively accessible $417/mo tier and SMS/phone at Enterprise is a genuine strength versus similarly-priced text-only competitors.
Resolution-based (not raw message) metering is a fairer usage model in principle, but the jump from Basic ($124) to Turbo ($417) to Enterprise ($1,499) is steep.
The few available reviews praise responsive support, but the sample size (a handful of G2 reviews, zero on Capterra) is too small to draw a confident conclusion either way.

pricing.model: Tiered SaaS by monthly resolutions and message credits

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: ~10 resolutions/mo, 20 credits, 50 webpages stored, 1 AI Agent, human handover, basic integrations, embeddable widget

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: ~1,000 resolutions/mo, 5,000 credits/mo, 1,000 webpages/agent, 2 AI Agents, 3 team seats, 2 chat workflows, self-improving agents, basic analytics

plans.name: Turbo
plans.notes: ~5,000 resolutions/mo, 25,000 credits/mo, 2,500 webpages/agent, 4 AI Agents, advanced analytics, voice agent, helpdesk integrations, priority support

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Custom resolution capacity and storage, bulk message discounts, SOC 2 & HIPAA compliance, custom integrations, SSO, SMS and phone agents

pricingBreakdown: Wonderchat's resolution-based billing — Basic at $124/mo for 1,000 resolutions, Turbo at $417/mo for 5,000 — is a fairer usage unit than Chatbase's raw message-credit model in principle, since you're not penalized for a chatbot that takes three back-and-forth messages to resolve one question. But the jump from Basic to Turbo is steep, nearly 3.4x the price for 5x the resolutions, and Turbo's $417/mo lands almost exactly between Chatbase's Standard ($120/mo) and Pro ($400/mo) tiers — except Wonderchat throws in a voice agent at that price point, something Chatbase doesn't offer until deep into Standard-tier telephony features and something Intercom doesn't offer without a $132/seat/mo Expert-tier commitment plus per-resolution Fin costs stacked on top. That makes Turbo a genuinely interesting value proposition on paper, but it's worth remembering this is reportedly a roughly two-person, bootstrapped company setting these prices — there's no G2 or Capterra review volume yet to confirm the voice agent holds up in practice the way there is for Chatbase or Tidio's equivalent features. Enterprise at $1,499/mo is a steep cliff from Turbo's $417/mo, more than triple the price for custom capacity — if you're anywhere near needing that tier, get Wonderchat's sales team to explain exactly what breaks the $417/mo ceiling for your specific volume before signing anything.

capabilities.note: Resolution-based metering (not raw message counts) plus self-improving agents from the Basic tier up is a thoughtful design in principle — you're paying for outcomes, not chat volume. The honest caveat is that the independent review base is thin enough (a handful of G2 reviews, none on Capterra) that real-world AI quality is harder to verify here than for better-reviewed competitors.

Training runs on business documents and uploaded files, scaling from 50 webpages on Free to 2,500 per agent on Turbo. It's a straightforward, quick setup according to the reviews that exist, but there simply isn't enough independent review volume yet to say how it holds up against a documentation-heavy site the way SiteGPT's larger page ceiling has been tested.

A voice agent is included starting at Turbo ($417/mo) and SMS/phone agents arrive at Enterprise — genuinely broader channel coverage than several similarly-priced AI chatbot competitors offer at any price. This is arguably Wonderchat's most distinctive capability, worth weighing against the thin review base rather than dismissing outright.

Human handover is built into every tier, including Free, so there's never a hard wall between the AI and a human picking up the conversation. That said, this is escalation logic, not a full team-inbox product — don't expect the routing, assignment, or reporting depth of a dedicated shared-inbox platform.

pros: Resolution-based pricing is arguably a fairer usage metric than raw message-count billing used by some competitors
Voice agent capability included at a mid-tier price point ($417/mo) rather than gated behind custom enterprise pricing
Fast, low-friction setup for training an agent on existing business documentation
Human handover available even on the free tier, avoiding a hard wall between AI and human support at every price point
cons: Very small independent review base (a handful of reviews on G2, none on Capterra) makes it hard to verify quality claims at scale
Bootstrapped, reportedly tiny team (~2 people) raises real questions about long-term support capacity and platform continuity
Steep jump in price between tiers ($124 to $417 to $1,499/mo) with less granularity than larger competitors offer
Free tier's 10 resolutions/month is only useful for the lowest-traffic trial scenarios

sentiment.quote: It allows me to train assistants with specific business information and deploy them quickly without a complex technical setup.

bestFor: Small businesses wanting resolution-based (rather than per-message) AI chatbot pricing
Teams wanting voice-agent capability without paying full enterprise pricing for it
Early-stage buyers comfortable evaluating a young, thinly-reviewed vendor directly rather than relying on review-site consensus
Businesses needing quick document-to-chatbot deployment without complex technical setup
verdict: Wonderchat's resolution-based pricing and mid-tier voice agent are genuinely appealing on paper — paying per successfully-resolved conversation instead of per raw message is a fairer unit, and getting a voice agent at $417/mo instead of gated behind a custom enterprise quote is a real value angle few competitors match at that price. The honest caveat, and it's a real one, not a formality: 'the handful of reviewers who've weighed in' is doing a lot of work in that sentence — G2 shows only a few reviews and Capterra shows none, which is a meaningfully thinner track record than Chatbase or Tidio carry into this comparison, and I can't independently verify the voice agent holds up at real volume the way I can for competitors with hundreds of reviews behind them. There's also the size question worth being upfront about: this is reportedly a roughly two-person, bootstrapped team setting enterprise-tier prices up to $1,499/mo, and that's a real continuity risk to weigh against a product that otherwise looks well-designed. My honest take: this is a reasonable pick if you're genuinely willing to be an early adopter with a small vendor and you've already priced out the alternative of waiting for more review volume to accumulate — it's not yet a proven-at-scale choice the way its better-reviewed competitors are, and you should go in knowing that's the trade you're making.
